To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

salt-dependent hypertension in the Dahl salt-sensitive rat is characterized by the development of intimal lesions, and the severity and extent of the lesions depend on the level and duration of salt intake.

1) the development of aortic lesions in Dahl S rats is dependent on the amount of salt consumed and the severity of the associated hypertension; 2) the extent and severity of the lesions correlate more closely with the rate and duration of hypertension than with the level reached by the end of the study; and 3) endothelial lesions are not a prominent feature in the development of atherosclerotic lesions in Dahl S hypertensive rats.

salt-induced hypertension in the Dahl salt-sensitive (S)-rat is associated with the development of intimal lesions, characterized by subendothelial accumulation of an electron-dense material, subendothelial lymphoid cell infiltration, and subendotheial fibrin deposition, which is not directly related to the level of salt consumption.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms responsible for the pathologic alterations in the arterial wall of hypertensive animals.
the pathophysiology of salt-induced hypertension in the Dahl rat.
the role of salt intake and salt sensitivity in hypertension, and the morphologic and ultrastructural characteristics of vascular lesions associated with hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the morphological changes of hypertension are the result of the interplay of several factors, and the nature of the lesions is dependent not only on the magnitude of the blood pressure elevation but also on other factors such as rate, duration of hypertension, the type of hypertension (e.g., malignant, accelerated, etc.), and the pathophysiologic mechanism of hypertension.
salt intake is a major factor in the development and progression of hypertension and atherosclerosis.
salt intake is a major determinant of the rate of hypertension and vascular lesions in the Dahl salt-sensitive model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
salt-sensitive Dahl rats develop hypertension and vascular lesions when they are fed a high-salt diet.

the aorta of salt-sensitive Dahl rats fed a high-salt diet develops lesions similar to those of human essential hypertension, including intimal lesions with lymphoid cells in the SES and endothelial abnormalities.
the vascular changes are not only related to the severity of hypertension, but also to its rate of development and the duration of hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the aortic media of S Dahl rats fed a high-salt diet thickens in a salt dose- and time-dependent fashion.
salt intake and salt sensitivity are important determinants of vascular lesions in hypertensive rats, which are not necessarily related to blood pressure levels.
endothelial injury and dysfunction are the primary cause of vascular disease, and that the endothelium is the primary target of salt in salt-sensitive hypertension.
